claim: An interrupt between a hook's OUT 0x243B and IN 0x253B leaves another NextREG selected, so the main line reads the wrong register; do the pair with interrupts off or have every interrupt reselect NR 7.
limit: A lockstep verifier must model NextREG or it answers IN 0x253B with game input.

evidence.text: HLIB_SPEED_IN latched a line number as the clock. Fix: pace held in every interrupt and NR 7 selected again before it returns.
Same race showed as a lone 175 ms update once in about 1,500; found via pace tables. The replay now checks the latched clock.
An interrupt left NR 0x53 selected and its page was latched as the speed, so the game ran at 28 MHz until reset.
The mutation selector is now latched inside the entry DI window; boundary injection caught the old version while register/R and RAM still matched.
The lockstep verifier fed port reads from the recording, so IN 0x253B returned a game input; it now answers 0x253B from its NextREG model.
The race check m3b_race covers MMU register reads under DI.
